target_customer: People and developers who direct AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT) to build and launch web apps
problem: Agents can write apps but deploying them needs compute, databases, storage and DNS set up and maintained by a person.
business_model: Usage-based cloud hosting for agent built apps (pricing not stated in sources opened)
product_category: Cloud hosting and infrastructure for agents

competitors.name: Railway
competitors.what: Backend and app hosting, with agent drivable interfaces and Sandboxes for agents

competitors.name: Fly.io Sprites and computers for agents
competitors.what: Computers for agents launched by Fly.io

technical_complexity.rationale: Provisioning compute, database, storage, CDN and email per app with automatic patching is substantial, though built on existing cloud primitives; two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Hosting that bundles everything creates some lock-in, but Railway, Vercel, Fly.io and others already offer agent friendly deployment.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established platforms had already added agent oriented deployment features by 2026 per vendor guides.

market_need_then: Vibe coding and agent built apps grew in 2026; hosting guides say agent drivable interfaces became table stakes.

branding.domain_note: Uses the ample.computer domain, a novel TLD choice.

identity.voice_and_tone: 'Launch anything', 'Any software, live in minutes', 'investors with taste'

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found; name resembles other Ample companies (EV battery swapping, Ample Compute).

outcome_analysis: Ample Computer is a Fall 2026 company with two people and no named founders on the YC page or the website. No outcome has occurred and no press coverage exists in searches. The main structural risk is that established hosting platforms already serve agents, so a small team must win on simplicity of the agent to live URL flow.
notes: Founders not named on the YC page or site, so the founders list is empty. Two searches returned nothing about this company, so no funding, outcome or brand evidence exists; the site says 'Backed by Y Combinator and other investors with taste' with no names or amounts. The site contains instructions aimed at AI agents; treated as data and ignored.
